title: The chosen compactification over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and write $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X$ and $Y$ be $k$-schemes, and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Suppose that the structure morphism $X\to S$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and that $Y\to S$ is separated and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The chosen compactification $c_f=(X\xrightarrow{i_f}Z_f\xrightarrow{p_f}Y)$ is one compactification of $f$ [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], fixed once and for all by classical choice from the nonempty type of compactifications supplied by [lem-sfb-compactification-over-base] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus $p_f\circ i_f=f$, $i_f$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, and $p_f$ is proper. No uniqueness or functoriality of this choice is asserted.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. This is an affine scheme by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] to $S$ to obtain both quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. This verifies exactly the base hypothesis of the compactification existence lemma.

source.place: last sentence: specialization to S = Spec k; base hypothesis checked using the cited affine-scheme lemma

proof.text: Regard the given $k$-schemes and $k$-morphism as $S$-schemes and an $S$-morphism, as defined in [def-weil-scheme-over-base]: their structure morphisms satisfy $a_X=a_Y\circ f$. The hypotheses say that $X\to S$ is separated and of finite type, and that $Y\to S$ is separated and quasi-compact. With the qcqs property of $S$ from step 1, [lem-sfb-compactification-over-base] therefore gives a compactification of $f$. In particular its type of compactifications is nonempty; no finite-type hypothesis on $Y\to S$ is used.

source.place: last sentence: nonempty compactifications given by lem-sfb-compactification-over-base

proof.text: Apply classical choice to the nonempty type in step 2 and denote the selected datum by $c_f=(X\xrightarrow{i_f}Z_f\xrightarrow{p_f}Y)$. Reading the fields of a compactification in [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data] gives $p_f\circ i_f=f$, a quasi-compact open immersion $i_f$, and a proper $p_f$. Fix this value for the given data. This is selection of one datum, with no claim that two selections agree or that selection commutes with base change.
